uiTranslations.AM_description:
I'm KosmicTeal, a developer with "Swiss-knife" experience on various programming languages such as C#, C++, Java, python, and HTML5/CSS among others; alongside working with Virtualization software such as VirtualBox and Docker.
I also have some knowledge on creating add-ons for spreadsheets and office automation systems such as VBS (Excel) or JavaScript (HTML5 and Google Apps). 

Aside from this and as a hobby, I'm also an illustrator artist, 3D model creator and TTRPG player. Some of my personal projects have been fueled by developing apps and add-ons to make my hobbies more enjoyable.
uiTranslations.MA_description:
A small robot mascot I have created for this page (and also to show a bit of my hobby as an artist!). Their name is a pun on Wyvern (which is a common word for a dragon with arms but no legs) and AI. However, not the Artificial Intelligence type of AI, but more like Artistical Intelligence.

Pretty much as wAIvern, art and technology can go together hand in hand. This means that AI shouldn't be used to replace real artists or overuse it mindlessly, with no criteria on the output.
Be in programming, arts or anything that requires human engineering; if AI is taken in mind, it should be used ethically and critically.

I have plans to do more stuff with this fella so, be sure to check an eye from time to time here!

RAR.cardText: Web app that allows TTRPG players to do combat-oriented summaries of their Character Sheets.
RAR.modalDescription:
I am currently taking this as a hobby project so updates might come randomly from time to time. Feel free to report any bug or suggestion on its Github repository and I will tackle them when time allows me to do so.

That page has been done with React, Redux and other Open Source technologies. Detailed information about this project can be found on the About page.
RAR.credits: All product and company names are trademarks or registered trademarks of their respective copyright holders. No copyright has been infringed with this application.

WEB.cardText: You're here. This card will show a bit of info about this website and its development.
WEB.modalDescription:
This website has had many revisions since its first creation in 2022.
Initially it was a static page using mainly HTML, CSS and Bootstrap UI as a base. Subsequently, on 14/01/2023 a button was added to switch between its Dark and Light theme.

Translations were added along with its rework in React and Vite on 08/26/2023; and an easter egg was added on 09/03/2023.

For its third version, the whole website has been reworked from scratch, taking advantage of the new Front-end knowledge, improving the interface and adding user interactions.

CTS.cardText: Overlay that allows you various tools to keep yourself focused while drawing on Clip Studio Paint.
CTS.modalDescription:
This software works as an overlay and sends inputs to your PC, emulating both modifier and arrow keys.
"Full Focus Mode", shown with a tablet icon, puts Clip Studio Paint on a "menu-less" mode, changes your Windows Settings for your taskbar's auto-hide while the mode is on and shows you a timewatch in case you want to keep track of your time without un-hiding your taskbar.
This app was created with a Surface platform in mind but it will also work on any other type of Tablet PC.

As a note, this app will always be in the middle right part of your screen, no matter if you're on Portrait or Landscape mode, and it can be hidden as you wish. It also has a special function that, if linked to a Pen Button action, you can open or close the app manually.
CTS.credits: Clip Studio Paint belongs to CELSYS.

ESD.cardText: Create new tracks by drag-and-dropping your Synthesizer V Studio banks into the engine.
ESD.modalDescription:
This software reads your SynthV database folder and allows you to drag-and-drop one of your databases (the last version you have installed) into SynthV to create a new track easily.

It just reads your folders, creates an empty file and allows you to drop it into the engine so it's safe to use.

As a small note, this is the first software that I've done that has DPI-awareness compatible animations and resizes perfectly depending on your screen.
ESD.credits: Synthesizer V Studio belongs to Dreamtonics.

KVMA.cardText: Group of applets that allow you to add some QoL in VirtualBox to save up opening the terminal.
KVMA.modalDescription:
These applets allow easy interaction with VirtualBox's vboxmanage.exe so users don't need to get into Windows' CMD.
During my learning period, I found myself with the need of access to some data or organize my Virtual Machines in an easy way. As we were also focusing on learning more about WinForms and Visual Studio, I decided to create these to make my learning a bit easier.

Currently there's two applets:

• VMIPCheck: Shows a Windows Notification with the main IP of your desired VM
• VMIconChange: UI-friendly applet that changes the icon of the VM you want instead of writing it on the terminal.

PSH.cardText: Customized Character Sheet for Roll20 that includes custom scripts and functional button rolls.
PSH.modalDescription:
Tailored character sheet built in HTML5, CSS and Javascript, based on a custom TTRPG (TableTop RolePlay Game) system.

Done as a gift for one of my best friends, this sheet was done mainly with CSS grids and calls towards Roll20's system. It also includes custom templates for dice rolls, inventory and abilities.

As it's done for a TTRPG game, it's also highly customizable and dynamic, so people can play it and improve it over time. As an extra, it's also compatible with Roll20's new Night Mode.
PSH.credits: Roll20 belongs to The Orr Group. TTRPG System created by @yaseiranryu. Beta-tested by @kurohaine97, @heniasama and @nise_loftsteinn. (Tw*tter accounts)

VOC.cardText: Standalone application that allows users to keep track of their Vocal Synthesizer Activation Codes.
VOC.modalDescription:
Small app that allows you to save your TTS (text-to-speech) Software activation codes and its installer locations.

Not as small as it looks like, because at the time it was the most extensive app I did and I wanted to push myself into learning something else UI-related aside WinForms. It also features some JSON mumbo-jumbo that would facilitate users to save their data easily.

It's not currently updated but you can input your data for a big chunk of released Voice Synthesizer softwares released from 2006 to 2021. All saved locally on your computer of course, no data breaches or such.
VOC.credits: Character thumbnails were done by LuxiayK. Each character belongs to their respective company.

VSP.cardText: "Quality of Life" plugins for various Signing Voice Synthesizers that allow scripting.
VSP.modalDescription:
Group of Plugins that were created in order to make music workflow easier on Singing Voice Synthesizers that allow scripting.

Vocal Synth's API was pretty restricting back in the time so, I couldn't let my imagination flow much, let alone when trying to find SDK/API from older software was close to impossible. However, I could do some requested addons by the community. Currently there's three addons:

• ListKeyNotes: Creates same-length notes in a specific key
• Crash-B-Gone for Tonio: Replaces all @ for V
• VocaAutoPitch (April Fools 2021): Adds the first four notes of Toby Fox's Megalovania from UNDERTALE.

LBS.cardText: Blender (2.8+) plugin set made in order to improve 3D model development's workflow.
LBS.modalDescription:
Group of Plugins that were adapted from existing code and adapted in order to make various 3D development tasks easier.

It took around a month to have the ensemble completed, as I was developing a model and I was tired of doing repetitive stuff manually. The main functionalities are:

• Mirroring .L Shapekeys and adding extra .L+.R ones
• Selecting Bones in order, connecting them and renaming the entire stack with the standard parent-child nomenclature
• Inverting the Bone tail axis, to be used with the previous functionality or by itself
• Renaming Bones and Vertex Groups from Standard Blender to Standard MikuMikuDance
• Adding Empty Objects that would later be understood by mmd_tools as Joints
LBS.credits: Blender belongs to Blender Foundation. Adapted from code snippets belonging to p2or, brockmann, Opponent019, batFINGER and Lemon from Blender's Stackexchange.

CS.cardText: Standalone application that enables users to edit the colours of their SynthV singer tracks.
CS.modalDescription:
Standalone app that was firstly created as a way to customize the colour of each "track" that was available on a Synthesizer V Studio project file without the need of any type of Plug-in.

This was done swiftly in an evening while trying to read how .svp files were generated and learning how to read and write data unto a JSON file. As by that time I only did program UIs with Windows Forms, I had to stick with that method for a good while.

Two years after the release of this project, Synthesizer V Studio's 1.10.0 release included a way to change the tracks colours directly from the interface itself.
CS.credits: Synthesizer V Studio belongs to Dreamtonics.

SPC.cardText: Plugin for Visual Studio Code that enables users to color-pick an accent colour to identify workspaces.
SPC.modalDescription:
This extension will allow you change your workspace activity bar and notifications' background colour easily! Just grab the mouse and select your desired colour in the color picker. This is also the first extension I've done for VSCode.

The main difference with other similar extensions is that it includes a classic colour picker so you can customise it without having to learn Hex colours.

Also, you can choose whether you want to extend this change to the Command Palette or Menu Bar, type the Hex colour manually in case you have a particular favourite colour or reset the changes to enjoy the chosen theme without any changes.
SPC.credits: Visual Studio Code belongs to Microsoft. Logo by LuxiayK. Code snippets by James Daniel (iro.js) and Sinan Aksay (Dynamic Text functions on Javascript).

PLS.cardText:
Homebrewed app that allows this precise page to be easily updated.
It looks pretty cool too.
PLS.modalDescription:
This application allows this website to be easily updateable.

Since its remake from plain HTML5/CSS to React+Vite, the data on this website is handled via JSON files. As manually writing JSON files can be a bit tiring, let alone translating them, I developed a WPF app to make my workflow easier.

It's still a bit rough on the edges, hence why it's only an "in-house" tool. Future planned updates are to allow deletion of data, buttons focused on making the workflow even faster, addition of new languages and translating some non-project data as well.

As of today, this application has been deprecated in favor of Planisphere2.
PLS.credits: Interface made with MahApps.Metro's NuGet package.

PLS2.cardText: Homebrewed app that allows this precise page to be easily updated, but better!
PLS2.modalDescription:
Taking advantage of the new knowledge I've been acquiring about Redux, React and other different libraries, I finally decided to update and improve a bit the previous version of Planisphere, switching from C# to TS.

This version has a cleaner and more useful interface, is faster and more optimized, and also allows now to add languages, frameworks and platforms; besides being able to change the theme with nothing to worry about.

Due to browser security limitations, I was not able to reimplement opening the final project with VSCode or opening a whole project by selecting the folder in all browsers, so it has been replaced by options similar to those made in the initial Windows version.
To make development easier with this site, I've also created a Standalone version with Tauri.

ENQ.cardText: The five elements have to converge into a single one. RPG game done in Godot.

BOD.cardText: Customizable and stylish components for React. Break the conventions.

SMR.cardText: Lightweight Windows application that manually changes the Slate/Landscape Mode
SMR.modalDescription:
Back in Windows 10, you could manually toggle Tablet mode in compatible PCs. This was removed on Windows 11, opting for a check whenever a Keyboard was recognized on the OS. 

For some reason on my PC, it doesn't automatically swap when I don't have my Keyboard connected so, I did this small app to do the change manually.

This app can work alongside ClipTheSurface to enable easier switches between Slate modes.

UUP.cardText: GNOME extension that allows you to see your PC's uptime directly from your top task bar
UUP.modalDescription:
This GNOME extension allows you to see your PC's uptime directly from your top task bar. Quite easy and lightweight.

It was created originally because conky wouldn't properly load on my Ubuntu environment so, after several tries, I decided to directly get the only thing I was interested; which is to see how many hours have I been programming.
UUP.credits: GNOME belongs to The GNOME Project.
